pick.motion: This house believes engineers should read only the risky pull requests closely and skim the rest.
pick.brief: Warp has published an open-source skill, /merge-risk, that agents can run on any pull request "to evaluate alignment, impact, verification, rollback cost, and error detection". Alignment checks the change sticks to its issue and flags drive-by edits. Impact flags sensitive paths such as auth, permissions, payments, personal data, migrations, dependencies and infrastructure. Verification checks that tests cover the behaviour and that user-facing changes come with proof such as screenshots. Rollback cost "separates reversible two-way doors from destructive or hard-to-undo changes". Error detection checks whether logs, monitoring and alerts would show a failure. The scores are meant to "focus human attention on the most important changes". A similar /pr skill by Matt Pocock, updated on 5 October 2026, asks each PR to state its "merge danger" and says to "skim a two-way door with a small blast radius, and read a one-way door slowly", while warning that the agent's own door call needs the closest check. Neither page gives numbers on review time or missed bugs.

backup.motion: This house believes coding teams should switch to a new model as soon as it beats the old one on benchmarks.
backup.brief: On 9 November 2026 Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, "the same underlying model": Fable is open to everyone with cyber and biology safeguards, and Mythos is limited to vetted organisations. Both cost $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, and Anthropic says output is "up to 30% faster" than Fable 5.1. In Anthropic's own table, Fable 5.2 at its highest effort scores 49.1% on FrontierCode 2.0 against 45.5% for Opus 5.5, and at high effort scores 45.3% at "roughly half the cost per task". It also leads on FrontierSWE v2 (69.9% vs 62.3%) and Terminal-Bench-Science (74.6% vs 58.7%). Opus 5.5 leads on one row, AA-Briefcase (1800 vs 1785). Anthropic says Fable's safeguards "will block most cybersecurity-related tasks". All scores are the vendor's own; the page gives no results from independent tests or from teams' own codebases.
